answer: The ledger admits a key only if an account over 200 epochs old posts a 50-token bond for it, capped at three keys per 100 epochs. Age accrues one epoch at a time, so it cannot be rented, reset or grown in parallel; a harbor scheduler's 300 epochs exist once. A fraud proof, such as two keys filing identical pigment assays, slashes every bond in that subtree. The n-th fake thus risks n×50 tokens, and an ivory-permit checker sponsoring clones loses all.
